content: Thrombotic events that are clinically symptomatic are rare but represent serious complications in neonates receiving intensive care. The majority of these thrombotic events are associated with the use of central vascular catheters. When symptomatic thrombosis occurs, it can lead to significant morbidity, including irreversible damage to organs and, in some cases, the loss of limbs. The purpose of this review was to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of thrombolytic agents in the treatment of arterial and venous thromboses in neonates. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted across multiple databases, including the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CINAHL, covering studies published from January 1966 to January 2004. Additionally, the authors reached out to experts and authors of relevant review articles to identify any unpublished studies. The inclusion criteria for this review were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or quasi-randomized controlled trials that compared thrombolytic agents with either heparin therapy or no treatment (observation) in neonates diagnosed with symptomatic arterial or venous thromboses. Two independent reviewers conducted the search and screening process. Despite an extensive search and efforts to contact authors for unpublished data, no eligible studies were identified. As a result, no randomized controlled trials or quasi-randomized controlled trials were available for analysis. Given the absence of eligible studies, no definitive conclusions could be drawn regarding the efficacy or safety of thrombolytic agents in this population. The authors emphasize the urgent need for a well-designed randomized controlled trial to compare thrombolytic therapy with heparin therapy. Such research is essential to provide neonatologists with evidence-based guidance for the management of arterial and venous thromboses in neonates.
